question.text: Central KYC Registry (CKYC) was established to:

answer.text: Create a centralized repository of KYC records to avoid duplication and enable interoperability across financial sector regulators
Replace SEBI as the KYC verification authority
Store only bank account KYC details
Enable trading without any KYC requirements

explanation.text: The Logic: The Central KYC Registry (CKYC), set up under the Prevention of Money Laundering Rules and operated by CERSAI, functions as a centralized repository of KYC records for clients in the Indian financial sector. Once a client's KYC is uploaded and a CKYC identifier is issued, other regulated entities — across securities, banking, insurance and other financial-sector regulators — can rely on those records, avoiding duplicate KYC collection and improving interoperability. The Trap: CKYC does not replace SEBI's KYC oversight, does not store only bank KYC details, and certainly does not allow trading without KYC; it sits alongside the regulators as a shared records repository. Note: The CKYC / Central KYC Registry concept is not described in the cited NISM Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook pages on KYC/UCC; the explanation above reflects general AML/KYC framework knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
